evidence.finding: Only 10:15 and 10:45 were below the 80% target, and service level recovered to 84.5% and 92.3% in the immediately following intervals.
The two misses were 75.0% with 48.7-second ASA at 10:15 and 77.4% with 47.7-second ASA at 10:45.
Offered calls were 97 versus 79 forecast at 10:15 and 93 versus 76 forecast at 10:45, aligning both misses with temporary above-forecast demand.
Total demand was 1,258 calls versus 1,216 forecast for the full window, an increase of approximately 3.5%, so demand was only moderately elevated overall rather than a sustained surge.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49 agents; productive staffing stayed within 44–46 agents and recovered immediately after its isolated low.
Underperformance rotated among queues while other queues remained healthy, indicating short-lived queue-level demand variability rather than a persistent center-wide capacity failure.
No routing, platform, or other operational event was recorded during the evaluation window.

primary_root_cause_detail: The alert reflects two isolated 15-minute service-level misses rather than a sustained operational incident. Service level fell to 75.0% at 10:15 and 77.4% at 10:45 during localized volume peaks, but recovered above target in the following intervals; aggregate window service level was approximately 86.2%.
recommended_actions: Apply alert persistence or rolling-window criteria so isolated 15-minute misses do not trigger material-incident classification.
Monitor intraday queue demand and use flexible cross-queue staffing when short-lived volume concentrations emerge.
Retain the existing staffing plan, while reviewing whether small real-time reserve capacity is warranted for approximately 20% interval-level forecast deviations.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Demand was elevated at the two miss intervals, but total window volume was only about 3.5% above forecast and the impact was not sustained.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in throughout the window, with productive staffing stable at 44–46.
Adherence remained approximately 89.8%–93.9% without a sustained decline corresponding to the service-level misses.
Center AHT remained near forecast and was 373.1 seconds at 10:15 and 381.1 seconds at 10:45, providing no sustained handle-time escalation.
Queue performance diverged temporarily, but the affected queue rotated and recovered; there is no persistent staffing imbalance sufficient to establish a material incident.
No routing-change event was supplied, and queue totals reconcile to center-level offered and answered volumes.
There was no platform event or evidence of call-processing disruption.
Forecast error was small across the full window despite two localized volume peaks.
Reported service levels recalculate correctly from answered-within-threshold and eligible offered calls, and call counts reconcile.

stakeholder_summary: CC-014 was not a sustained material incident. Two isolated service-level misses coincided with temporary above-forecast interval demand, while staffing, adherence, AHT, routing, platform health, and metric integrity showed no causal failure. Performance recovered promptly and remained above target on an aggregate-window basis.
